Markets often miss second order implications until it shows up in direct statements. 

- If $LITE is completely sold out... (largely due to $NVDA bottlenecking everyone else, eg. securing Greensboro capacity), where else do your other companies like $AMD / hyperscalers / etc. get their supply procurement? 

- $SIVE is coming online with like 1/6th of the world's current laser capacity by themselves. (100M+ cw dfb lasers vs. 608M EML/CW globally per Trendforce). 

Not even including their partner foundries that they're targeting 2:1 for. 

- $AAOI is coming online with a ton of capacity too next year enough to produce 400k ELSFP + $471m/month of transceivers. 

Then combine that with other supply chain statements like "Having 2-3 suppliers used to be the norm, now it is 5-7" from Lightcounting.

So as long as your products actually work + can scale, it's hard to see anyone else with capacity not get qualified into your supply chains. 

Since optical component shortages are a massive bottleneck now.

So as long as your products actually work + can scale, it's hard to see anyone else with capacity not get qualified into your supply chains. 

Since optical component shortages are a massive bottleneck now.

Third Day Token2049

> Third day/last day, literally the most exciting day of Token2049 because we had all the AI builders, VCs, devs in the room with us at gm AI v2

> Conversations shift to AI, privacy, robotics, DePIN, decentralization, tokenomics, all the geeky stuff that I couldn't find anywhere else at Token2049

> Surprisingly, I've met even more teams who have been around for a long time and are pivoting into new interesting directions

> Some pivot to focus on Chinese AI market, moving their office to Shenzhen. Some pivot to AI x Gaming x Consumer Content while others move to social trading and privacy AI

> Was quite surprised to see CT freaking out over Quantum. No one (I mean no one) at Token2049 talks about Quantum at all. 

> People who are bearish are bearish because of macro + some believe it's the end of the 4-year cycle. People who are bullish believe in the institutionalization & the acceptance of crypto as the global financial backbone, merging with TradFi

> Builders on the other hand are much more concerned about the business side of things. "How do we get users to spend more?" "How do we really use tokens in a way that align interest & drive growth?" "How do we accelerate GTM with x402?". This feels like a breathe of fresh air. Less degeneracy, more fundamental product building

All in all, pretty happy with how the day turned out. Got a few good research ideas in fairly new sectors that I haven't seen anyone talk about yet on CT.

If you were to ask me "what's the SINGLE best thing I got out of Token2049?"

It's the confirmation that Onchain/Decentralized AI is (and will continue to be) the most asymmetrical and one of the fastest growing sectors in crypto in the next 2 years

Excited to share some of my deeper findings (interesting narratives & projects) in my upcoming Token2049 Article which I'll drop tomorrow

How's your Token2049 experience?
